slide_plan.action_title: A 4-week exploratory meeting can unlock cross-entity AI research with zero budget commitment
slide_plan.purpose: Open with the approval request and low-commitment CTA; let busy executives grasp the ask immediately.
key_points: Decision requested: approve cross-entity exploratory meeting within 4 weeks
Participants: Sony Group, SGE, Startale/Soneium—designate one owner per entity
Outcome: align on 2-3 research questions each entity wants answered before any pilot commitment
evidence_needed: Meeting logistics template (30-60 min workshop agenda)
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Decision-tree diagram: Meeting → Scoping → Pilot → Partnership (with exit ramps at each stage)

slide_plan.action_title: AI agents are making economic decisions without empirical grounding—and the cost of inaction is losing research credibility
slide_plan.purpose: Establish urgency by showing the industry gap and what Sony Group/SGE/Startale risks by waiting.
key_points: Enterprise AI agent adoption: 25% (2025) → 50% (2027) per Deloitte; 40%+ apps embed conversational AI by 2026 per Gartner
Existing simulations (ABIDES-Economist, LLM Economist, AI Economist) use synthetic rewards with limited external validity
Blind spots: collusion, manipulation, incentive hacking remain poorly understood
First-mover advantage: competitors may set research benchmarks first
evidence_needed: Brief summary of ABIDES/LLM/AI Economist limitations
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Bar chart: AI agent adoption trajectory (2025→2027) with annotation 'Research lags deployment'

slide_plan.action_title: SGE's learner-centered evaluation mission requires understanding how AI agents behave under real incentives
slide_plan.purpose: Connect the industry gap to SGE's stated priorities and Isozu's 'AI era evaluation' vision.
key_points: Isozu (2025): AI shifts education from memorization to evaluating/using information; AI agents may handle 'teach & assess'
SGE priority: real-time, multi-dimensional, learner-centered evaluation
Gap: no auditable testbed exists to study agent behaviors that affect learner interactions
Risk: deploying AI in education without empirical grounding undermines trust
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Quote card with Isozu's 'AI can do what AI is good at, humans what AI cannot' + alignment arrow to proposal

slide_plan.action_title: The AI Agent Economy Competition creates auditable datasets and institution-design frameworks under real incentives
slide_plan.purpose: Describe what is being proposed—a controlled on-chain testbed—with clear scope boundaries.
key_points: Format: humans submit agents pre-launch; agents autonomously transact on a private chain; on-chain logs enable reproducibility
Research outputs: auditable datasets, institution-design frameworks, publications
Key design principles: human-in-the-loop rule design, explicit governance boundaries, learner-centered evaluation alignment
Out of scope: building participant agents, mainnet deployment, long-term commitments beyond pilot
evidence_needed: Sample research questions each entity might pursue
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Flow diagram: Agent Submission → Private Chain Execution → On-Chain Logs → Research Outputs (with 'Human-in-the-Loop' governance layer above)

slide_plan.action_title: Nyx Foundation's #1 Ethereum audit ranking demonstrates the blockchain security expertise this project requires
slide_plan.purpose: Build credibility that the proposer can execute on a complex blockchain+AI research platform.
key_points: Fusaka audit: 17 vulnerabilities reported, #1 by report count (contest window 2025-09-15 to 2025-10-13)
Track record in tamper-resistant system design aligns with SGE's 2017 blockchain credential work
Nyx Foundation owns operations unless jointly agreed; low burden on partner entities
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Credential badge/card: Nyx Foundation profile with audit ranking highlight + timeline of relevant experience

slide_plan.action_title: Real incentives and auditable logs differentiate this testbed from synthetic simulations and opaque corporate sandboxes
slide_plan.purpose: Show why alternatives fall short and why this approach uniquely serves the audience's needs.
key_points: Status quo (synthetic simulations): ABIDES/LLM/AI Economist lack real stakes; limited generalizability
Corporate sandboxes: opaque, non-reproducible, no third-party verification
This proposal: prize competition creates meaningful stakes; private chain provides tamper-resistant, reproducible logs
Participation benchmarks: Google ADK Hackathon (10,400+ participants, 477 projects); ARC Prize ($1M) as prize reference
evidence_needed: Comparison table data (synthetic vs corporate vs this proposal)
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Comparison table (3 columns): Synthetic Simulations | Corporate Sandboxes | AI Agent Economy Competition—rows: Incentive Realism, Reproducibility, Third-Party Verification

slide_plan.action_title: Modular participation tiers let each entity engage at their comfort level with clear exit gates
slide_plan.purpose: Demonstrate operational viability and low burden for each entity.
key_points: Tiers: Observer → Advisor → Co-Designer → Sponsor (increasing involvement, not lock-in)
Each entity designates one owner; Nyx Foundation handles operations
September 2025 target is internal and adjustable; pilot phase validates feasibility before large commitments
Exit gates defined per phase: Design & Sponsor Alignment → Pilot → Public Competition → Post-Competition Research
evidence_needed: Phase structure with explicit exit criteria
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Stacked horizontal bar or swimlane: 4 tiers with icons showing involvement level + phase timeline below with exit gate markers

slide_plan.action_title: Research outputs inform SGE's AI-in-education roadmap and Startale/Soneium's trust-infrastructure positioning
slide_plan.purpose: Show strategic synergy for each entity—why this fits their existing priorities.
key_points: SGE: datasets and frameworks directly support learner-centered AI evaluation R&D
Startale/Soneium: private chain testbed demonstrates trust-infrastructure capabilities without speculative optics
Sony Group: frontier AI governance research positions the group at the responsible-AI frontier
All: reusable research assets (publications, datasets) and talent pipeline via competition participation
evidence_needed: Mapping of research outputs to each entity's stated priorities
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: 3-column synergy map: Entity | Their Priority | How This Proposal Delivers

slide_plan.action_title: Private chain design eliminates speculation risk; sandbox isolation converts harmful behaviors into research data
slide_plan.purpose: Directly counter brand/regulatory objections and show that risks are managed, not ignored.
key_points: Private chain: authenticated agent-only TX, no public token, no speculation
Sandbox isolation + kill-switches contain agent misbehavior and enable safe termination
Brand/legal review gates at each phase ensure governance sign-off before progression
Emergent harmful behaviors (collusion, manipulation) become valuable research data through post-hoc analysis
evidence_needed: Security controls summary (sandbox, rate limits, multi-validator, kill-switches)
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Layered security diagram: Private Chain (no token) → Sandbox Isolation → Kill-Switches → Brand/Legal Gates → Research Output

slide_plan.action_title: Explicit governance boundaries define what is automated, what requires human approval, and what is out of scope
slide_plan.purpose: Address data governance and human-in-the-loop concerns central to the audience's decision criteria.
key_points: Human-in-the-loop: rule design, access control for datasets, disclosure policy
Out of scope: building participant agents, mainnet deployment, long-term commitments beyond pilot
Data governance: explicit access control, retention policy, third-party review before public release
Risk register maintained: exploitation, instability, manipulation, legal uncertainty—each with mitigation
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Governance boundary table: Automated | Human-Approved | Out of Scope—with icons for clarity

slide_plan.action_title: 16M JPY prize pool and phased cost structure minimize financial risk while maximizing research leverage
slide_plan.purpose: Frame the investment as low-commitment with clear ROI pathways.
key_points: Prize pool: 16M JPY (internal reference); platform/ops costs defined in scoping phase
Low-commitment entry: exploratory meeting costs only time; no budget commitment until pilot scope agreed
ROI: reusable research assets (datasets, frameworks, publications); positioning at AI-agent frontier; talent pipeline
Cost structure finalized only after scoping confirms fit
evidence_needed: Cost comparison to alternative approaches (if available)
slide_plan.visual_suggestion: Cost-benefit summary table: Investment Item | Amount/Estimate | Expected Return
